title: fast-path-demo-to-production-price-messaging
content:
Objective:
- Produce a compact set of messaging variants (elevator + hero paragraph + quickstart script + pricing phrasing) engineers respond to when evaluating hosted inference. Focus = low friction -> measurable progress in first 30 minutes; predictable unit economics thereafter.

Audience:
- Individual engineers trying an integration in an afternoon
- Small eng teams validating a prototype for product leadership
- Platform/infra leads evaluating a production path (cost/latency predictability)

TL;DR (3x quick variants):
1) Developer-first: "Try inference in 5 minutes, ship in days." Emphasize single SDK, one API key, streaming responses, and sample app that runs locally then flips to hosted.
2) Predictable economics: "Transparent per-token billing + starter credits so you can measure cost against real traffic patterns before committing."
3) Enterprise-ready path: "Start hosted, scale to reserved or private with identical API and operational tooling."

Winning value threads (prioritized):
- Low friction to true signal: not just "hello world" but measurable prototype metrics in 30–60 minutes (latency, cost/1k tokens, concordance with eval set).
- Predictable unit economics: clear per-token math, cost examples for common patterns (chat, summarization, embeddings).
- Risk reduction for product teams: same API across hosted/dedicated/private -> easy upgrade path without rework.
- Observability that matters: per-route latency & cost, token-level breakdowns, and simple alerts you can wire to your existing monitoring.

Hero paragraph candidates (pick tone):
- Practical tone: "Redwood's Hosted API gets you from prototype to production without the plumbing: one SDK, streaming responses, and per-token pricing you can model in a spreadsheet. Start with starter credits, see real latency and cost metrics, then decide if you want dedicated capacity or a private deployment — the API stays the same."
- Conviction tone: "Build fast. Pay predictably. Stay in control. Redwood's Hosted API gives engineers a single, production-grade endpoint for generation, chat, and embeddings — instrumented for cost and latency so you never guess economics again."

Quickstart flow (30-minute playbook to include in docs and demo):
1) Sign up -> receive 2000 starter credits (experiment number; A/B test levels)
2) Install SDK: npm i @redwood/inference (show minimal snippet)
3) Run the quickstart sample that: sends a short chat prompt, streams tokens to console, stores latency & token counts in a minimal dashboard
4) Swap a single flag to route to a prebuilt sample app (hosted) so they can compare local vs hosted latency/cost
5) Export a 1-page cost snapshot: tokens used, avg latency, estimated monthly cost at 100k qpm (example numbers included in docs)

Concise quickstart script (for sales/dev advocates to read aloud):
- "We’ll get you a key, add the SDK in one line, run the sample app, and by the time your coffee’s done you’ll see streaming output and a cost snapshot that maps directly to your dashboard — no infra setup."

Pricing-language experiments (phrasing + concrete anchor ideas):
- Anchor language options: "per-1k tokens", "per-response", "per-embedding vector". Engineers respond better to token math with worked examples.
- Starter offers to test: 2000 credits free; or 30-day trial with 100k token/month allowance. Run parallel experiments.
- Transparent sample table (use in UI & docs):
  - Chat small (gpt-style short): $0.40 / 1k tokens
  - Chat medium (context windows): $0.90 / 1k tokens
  - Embeddings: $0.25 / 1k tokens
  - Note: numbers are experimental — run price elasticity tests.
- Price framing snippets:
  - "Estimate your bill in 3 clicks: we show tokens consumed per route and cost per 1k so you can model real product usage."
  - "Starter credits = risk-free signal. Pay-as-you-go after that; reserved capacity for teams that need predictability."

Positioning vs competitors (concise differentiator bullets):
- vs OpenAI-style marketplaces: focus on predictable unit economics and an upgrade path to private/dedicated without rework. Not a marketplace — a runtime and ops story.
- vs managed cloud endpoints (AWS/GCP): focus on developer ergonomics and out-of-the-box instrumentation for token-level cost visibility and eval hooks — fewer ops steps to meaningful signal.
- vs self-hosted vendors: emphasize time-to-signal (minutes -> hours) and frictionless scale; self-hosting wins on absolute control but loses on onboarding speed and dev experience.

Objection handling (short scripts):
- "We worry about cost": show live demo of token breakdown, cheapest generation modes, and how caching reduces bills. Offer to run a short smoke test on their representative traffic.
- "We're going to self-host later": explain identical API and rollout path; show migration checklist (one-liner).
- "Latency SLAs": show observable per-route p50/p95 and dedicated offerings with SLA.

Hypotheses to validate (tracking suggestions):
- H1: Engineers with a 2000-credit starter convert to second session 60% more than without credits. (track signups -> second session)
- H2: Providing a 1-click cost snapshot reduces abandonment during prototype evaluation by 25%. (track quickstart abandonment flow)
- H3: Pricing table with concrete worked examples increases perceived price clarity and reduces support contacts about billing by 40%.

Content/UX notes for docs and in-product microcopy:
- Show a "What this costs" panel next to code samples with worked examples for 1,000 responses, 10k responses.
- Use language: "tokens" over "requests" for accuracy; include an inline tooltip that translates tokens -> characters for non-technical PMs.
- Provide a "Cost lab" sample app they can fork: upload a prompt set, run 100 iterations, see token histogram and cost estimate.

Open questions / decision points (for PM/GTM review):
- Starter credit amount: 2000 vs 10k vs time-limited allowance. Which yields higher engagement? A/B test.
- Which pricing tiers to show by default in UI (min 3): opt for chat-basic, chat-pro, embeddings. Exact price points TBD.
- Tone test: practical vs aspirational hero paragraph — which converts better on signup CTA?

Next steps (who does what):
- Product content: add "Cost lab" sample + 1-click cost snapshot in docs (Priya) — due 2025-03-14
- Growth: implement starter credit A/B test (Marco) — due 2025-03-20
- Sales enablement: script recording and quick 2-min demo for AE playbook (Elena) — due 2025-03-10

Notes to self / rough copy snippets for experiments (quick stash):
- "Start free, measure cost, scale with confidence."
- "One API, three deployment modes — no rework when you need dedicated capacity."
- "See token spend live while you iterate on prompts."

References / links:
- internal: CONFLUENCE-1234 (hosted api pricing experiments), JIRA-GTM-88 (starter credit A/B), github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts#demo

Unresolved / handwavey metrics to validate during pilots:
- target conversion % from trial to paid after cost-lab: 8–12% (guestimate)
- acceptable monthly unit price band to highlight during pilot: $0.20–$1.00 / 1k tokens depending on model class

End of brief.

Inline TODOs (notes for editor):
- Replace sample price numbers with finance-approved ranges before external publish.
- Add short recording of quickstart for explainers page.
- Convert Quickstart flow into a 4-step checklist for in-product walkthrough.
